actions: depresses/protracts the scapula, elevates ribs 3-5 (accessory inspiration when the scapula is fixed)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Deep to pectoralis major; the axillary artery and brachial plexus cords pass directly behind it. More precisely, the cords' names (lateral/medial/posterior) are defined by their position relative to the axillary artery's 2nd part -- which is itself the segment of the artery running directly posterior to this muscle, so 'relative to pectoralis minor' is the standard shorthand for a relationship that is technically defined one step removed, via the artery (adjusted for precision after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.notes: Three-quarters of muscle length. The needle path crosses toward the chest wall and the underlying brachial plexus, which is why the source treats ultrasound as mandatory here.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part II -- Proximal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(6):276 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17060276 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites (Yi, Li, Yang, Moon and others)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transducer angled 45 degrees toward the axilla on the anterior thoracic wall, along the midclavicular line, about 5-6 cm distal to the clavicle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to pectoralis major, superficial to the rib cortex and intercostal muscles.
structures_at_risk: brachial plexus and axillary vessels (the underlying neurovascular bundle)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Also injected for pectoralis minor syndrome, where the overactive muscle compresses the distal brachial plexus branches beneath it -- the same bundle that is the hazard of the injection.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part II -- Proximal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(6):276 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17060276 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites (Yi, Li, Yang, Moon and others)

trigger_points.location_description: Trigger points in the belly under pectoralis major, at the level of the 3rd-4th rib; palpate through relaxed pectoralis major or via the axilla
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Anterior deltoid and pre-cordial/pectoral region, extending down the ulnar side of the arm and forearm to digits 3-5 -- a cardiac-pain and C8/ulnar mimic; true nerve entrapment adds neurogenic paraesthesiae, distinguishing it from pure referral.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Restricted end-range elevation and horizontal abduction (doorway stretch reproduces); rounded-shoulder posture; symptoms with backpack straps/hands-overhead sleep.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded shoulder muscle reference document (Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)

clinical.function_biomechanics: Draws the scapula forward and downward, tipping it anteriorly and rotating it internally/downward; stabilises the scapula against upward-rotation forces; accessory inspiration with the scapula fixed. A short resting pectoralis minor reproduces the impingement-type kinematics: persisting anterior tilt and greater internal rotation of the scapula during elevation — a key modifiable driver of subacromial symptoms and a first-line stretch/manual target.
clinical.adjacent_structures: Adjacent bursae: No constant named bursa; the subcoracoid bursa lies just lateral to its insertion. Adjacent structures — mutual influence: Compresses the plexus/axillary vessels beneath its tendon in hyperabduction — pectoralis minor syndrome, alone or with neurogenic TOS: anterior chest/axillary tenderness with arm pain/paraesthesiae; a simple tenotomy relieved ≥90% when PMS occurred alone in a 100-operation series. Coracoid transfer (Latarjet) detaches it; tight PM loads the ACJ and subacromial outlet; it shields (and blocks access to) level-II nodes.

trigger_points.location: TrPs in the belly under pectoralis major at the 3rd–4th rib level; palpate through relaxed pec major or via the axilla.
trigger_points.referred_pain: Anterior deltoid and pre-cordial/pectoral region, extending down the ulnar side of the arm and forearm to digits 3–5 — a cardiac-pain and C8/ulnar mimic; entrapment adds true neurogenic paraesthesiae, distinguishing it from pure referral.
trigger_points.source: Donnelly JM, Fernández-de-las-Peñas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds). Travell, Simons & Simons’ Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual. 3rd ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2019. Muscle chapters as named in each section.

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: Into the anterior chest/coracoid zone: pectoralis major (clavicular/sternal), scaleni, subclavius, sternalis
cervical discogenic pain (C6–C7) can project pre-cordially
cardiac ischaemia and its territory overlap — always risk-stratify first.
clinical.movement_restrictions_aggravators: Restricted end-range elevation and horizontal abduction (doorway stretch reproduces), rounded-shoulder posture, symptoms with backpack straps/hands-overhead sleep.
clinical.notes: Measure resting PM length/posture in every impingement; in “TOS”, block-test the pectoralis minor separately — a large subgroup is PM-only and curable with far smaller surgery.
clinical.caveat: Trigger-point locations and referral maps derive from the Travell–Simons clinical-observational tradition, now standardised by Delphi consensus criteria [32] and supported by prevalence and hyperalgesia studies in shoulder pain [30,31]; they are expert-level evidence, not trial-level, and inter-examiner reliability of TrP palpation is moderate. Facet, ACJ and subacromial referral patterns, by contrast, come from experimental provocation in volunteers/patients [33,34,37]. Textbook anatomy is cited at section level; where major texts disagree (segmental levels), the range is given and flagged. Figures and patterns older than 12 months are anatomical/physiological constants and are not considered stale.
